subject: ventures/brewery-excise-tax-calculator
professional: a brewery excise-tax compliance specialist (the bookkeeper or CPA who prepares TTB F 5000.24 Excise Tax Returns for craft breweries). They would check first: that the $3.50 / $16 / $18 tiers are applied cumulatively per calendar year with the 60,000 reduced-rate barrels counted inside the 6 million (26 U.S.C. 5051(a)(1)(C), (a)(2)(A)); that the $3.50 rate is limited to domestic brewers producing 2,000,000 barrels or fewer and shared across a controlled group; that package conversions to 31-gallon barrels are exact; and that the return-frequency hint matches 26 U.S.C. 5061(d)(4) / 27 CFR 25.164 (quarterly at <= $50,000, annual at <= $1,000, both on prior-year AND expected current-year liability)

evidence.correctness: Recomputed in an independent Python function written from 26 U.S.C. 5051(a) as amended by the CBMA (statute text cited from the auditor's knowledge; marisstella.app and government hosts were refused by the session proxy). Pass: sample input 101,175 gal / 31 = 3,263.7097 bbl, tax $11,422.98 (node plan(sampleInput()) identical); 70,000 bbl small brewer $370,000; 6.5M bbl small brewer $104,250,000 (60,000 x 3.50 + 5,940,000 x 16 + 500,000 x 18); 2.5M bbl non-small $40,000,000; FAQ per-package figures ($1.75/half keg, $0.254 and $1.161 per 24x12oz case, 4.57x ratio, 1.41 cents/pint) all reproduce; filing thresholds at $1,000.00/$1,000.01 and $50,000.00/$50,000.01 switch at the right edge. Fail: (1) the growth table keeps the $3.50 rate after volume passes 2M barrels: plan({otherBarrels:1000000, small:true}).growth at 3x shows $47,250,000 for 3,000,000 bbl where a brewer producing 3M bbl loses eligibility and owes $48,000,000 (calc.mjs:72); (2) a blank allotment field becomes 0, so plan({halfKegs:200, allotment:''}) returns $1,600 instead of $350 (4.6x) with only an advice line saying the share is 0 (calc.mjs:21,61). Core tier arithmetic is right in every recomputed case, so 3; the two failures are on secondary paths.
evidence.completeness: README/page features checked by running plan(): package-to-barrel conversion (works), three-tier tax (works), controlled-group allotment share (works, clamped to 60,000), per-package tax table (works, average rate), growth table (works, but see 2M defect), filing-frequency hint (works), CSV export via toCsv (works, labels with commas quoted), example loader (sampleInput works), usage counter local-only (usage.test.mjs passes). No TODOs or stubs. Served page not loadable from this session (proxy 403 on marisstella.app); sibling links (craft-brewery-batch-margin-calculator, brewery-tank-schedule-optimizer, self-employment-tax-calculator, distillery- and winery-excise-tax-calculator) all exist in ventures/.
evidence.verification: `cd ventures/brewery-excise-tax-calculator && node --test '*.test.mjs'`: 22 tests, 22 pass. Eight seeded mutations via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: 1 caught (t1 ignoring the allotment), 7 survived: quarterly threshold <= -> <, annual threshold x10, 12-oz case gallons 24*12/128 -> /124, marginal-rate boundary < -> <=, t2 cap 6M-t1 -> 6M (double-counts 60,000 bbl for a small brewer over 6M), t3 subtracting t1, and dropping the 60,000 allotment clamp. Tests assert one point per rule and nothing at the boundaries; no test covers a small brewer above 6M, any package other than half kegs, or the threshold edges.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (96 lines), index.html (181), page.test.mjs, calc.test.mjs, usage.mjs head. Pure, small, readable module with input validation and an error path. Defects: blank number fields silently become 0 (num(), calc.mjs:21) which for the allotment removes the reduced rate; allotment above 60,000 silently clamped with no message (calc.mjs:31); dead CSS copied from an hours-of-service tool (tr.drive/.break/.dwell/.off/.restart, textarea, index.html:25,33-35); advice prints '$3.5' rather than '$3.50' (calc.mjs:76,79).
evidence.claims: Checked: rates and thresholds in FAQ/JSON-LD and the 'rates this applies' list match 5051(a) (pass); '2 million barrels or fewer' matches 'not more than 2,000,000' (pass); per-keg/case FAQ numbers recomputed (pass); 'nothing is uploaded' backed by page.test.mjs (no fetch/XHR/sendBeacon) and usage.mjs localStorage-only (pass); not-modelled list (state tax, importers, contract brewing, tax-free removals, losses, refunds, actual return) present on page and README (pass); disclaimer and no-warranty footer present (pass). Partial: the filing FAQ says eligibility depends on expected liability only, omitting the prior-year condition, though hedged with 'generally' and 'confirm with TTB'. llms.txt links the github.io host, which the Pages build rewrites at deploy (source-only).
evidence.fitness: Walked the owner's job: enter a year's kegs/cases, read tax per keg and the 60,000-bbl cliff, export CSV. That works and is useful for pricing and expansion planning. The compliance specialist's actual job (a per-period F 5000.24: semimonthly or quarterly removals, running count against the 60,000 allotment across periods, netting beer returned to the brewery under 26 U.S.C. 5056, tax-free removals, transfer-in-bond receipts) is out of scope and stated as such; a professional would hit the lack of per-period allocation in the first hour. Hence 2.
evidence.domain: Compared with 26 U.S.C. 5051(a)(1)(A),(C) and (a)(2)(A) (CBMA rates, made permanent by the Taxpayer Certainty and Disaster Tax Relief Act of 2020), 26 U.S.C. 5061(d)(4) / 27 CFR 25.164 return periods, and the 31-gallon barrel (5051(a)(1)). Method matches: 60,000 reduced barrels counted inside the 6M, cumulative per calendar year, $18 above 6M, $3.50 limited to domestic producers <= 2M and shared in a controlled group, tax on removal not production. Departures: growth projection ignores loss of the reduced rate above 2M production; filing hint tests current-year liability only; the 6M $16 tier is also apportioned across a controlled group (5051(a)(1)(C) with the controlled-group rules) but the tool gives every non-small brewer the full 6M; the $16 rate assignment by foreign producers to importers and CBMA transfer-in-bond (26 U.S.C. 5414) are not modelled and transfer-in-bond is not named in the not-modelled list. Within its stated limits a practitioner would sign the method off.

mutations.change: const t1 = Math.min(barrels, reducedCap); -> Math.min(barrels, TIERS.reducedBarrels)
t2 cap TIERS.standardCap - t1 -> TIERS.standardCap (double-counts 60,000 bbl above 6M)
t3 = barrels - standardCap -> barrels - standardCap - t1

defects.what: Growth table multiplies volume up to 3x but keeps the small-brewer status, so a brewer projected past 2,000,000 barrels still gets $3.50 on 60,000 barrels: 1M bbl x3 shows $47,250,000 instead of $48,000,000, and the 'cost of growing' the tool is built to show understates the loss of the reduced rate. No warning either.

A cleared allotment field is read as 0 (num('') = 0), so a small brewer silently loses the reduced rate: plan({halfKegs:200, allotment:''}) gives $1,600 instead of $350. The only signal is an advice line saying the share is 0.

Seven of eight seeded mutations survive: no test at the $1,000/$50,000 filing edges, at the marginal-rate boundary, for a small brewer above 6M barrels (t2 cap), for the 60,000 clamp, or for any package size other than half kegs.
small=true is accepted with removals above 2,000,000 barrels and no warning that the reduced rate requires production of 2M or fewer.
Filing hint tests only the current-year estimate; 26 U.S.C. 5061(d)(4) / 27 CFR 25.164 also require prior-year liability under the threshold. Hedged with 'may be available' and 'confirm with TTB'.

The $16 tier's 6,000,000 barrels is shared across a controlled group like the 60,000, but only the 60,000 share is an input; transfer in bond (26 U.S.C. 5414), returns to the brewery (5056) and foreign-producer assignment of the $16 rate to importers are not modelled, and transfer in bond is not named in the not-modelled list.
Allotment above 60,000 is silently clamped with no message to the user.
Dead CSS copied from another tool (tr.drive/.break/.dwell/.off/.restart, textarea) and advice prints '$3.5' instead of '$3.50'.
llms.txt links the duncan-haywood.github.io host; the Pages build rewrites it at deploy (served page not loadable from this session to confirm).

verdict: A small, honest planning calculator whose core arithmetic is right: every recomputed tier total (70,000 bbl, 6.5M small, 2.5M non-small, the sample mix) and every FAQ per-package figure matches 26 U.S.C. 5051(a) as amended by the CBMA, and the page states its limits and disclaimer. It misses the bar on verification: 22 tests pass but 7 of 8 seeded bugs in the tier caps, boundaries, filing thresholds and package sizes survive. Two secondary outputs are wrong: the growth table keeps the $3.50 rate past 2M barrels of production, and a cleared allotment field silently becomes 0. Finished for what it claims; not a per-period F 5000.24 tool, which it says.
